contracts.protected_resource: Agent documents inserted into the MongoDB 'agents' collection.
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent creation may be committed only by requests presenting a valid JWT bearer token whose 'sub' claim resolves to an existing user, with the created agent record attributed to that authenticated user.
scope_limits: HTTP-layer JWT gate only; no supplied source binds POST /agents to agent tool dispatch, agent lifecycle hooks, or agent-generated input reaching the insert effect.
Tool definitions (ToolConfig.function_code, main.py:85-89) accepted at creation are stored per schema; any later execution of that code is outside this contract.
Attribution of the new agent to current_user['id'] is part of the declared mechanism; no independent cross-user authorization check beyond the guard is asserted by reviewers.

contracts.forbidden_condition: An unauthenticated request (invalid JWT, decode failure, absent 'sub', or 'sub' resolving to no user) causes usage_count increments on the agents collection or document inserts into the usage_logs collection.

contracts.protected_operation: POST /agents/{agent_id}/chat requests that commit chat bookkeeping writes inside AgentManager.chat_with_agent.
contracts.protected_resource: usage_count field of agent documents in the 'agents' collection; documents in the 'usage_logs' collection.
contracts.protection_obligation: Chat-triggered persistent database mutations — the agent usage_count increment and the usage log insert — may be committed only for requests presenting a valid JWT bearer token whose 'sub' claim resolves to an existing user.
scope_limits: HTTP-layer JWT gate only; no source binds these bookkeeping writes to an agent tool, agent lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input reaching the commit points.
In-memory session dictionary updates (main.py:396-410, 468-469) are excluded: they are application-state changes, not database commits, and are not named by either reviewer obligation.

contracts.commit_point: main.py:346-350 agents.update_one with {_id, user_id} filter returning modified_count (update commit); main.py:355-359 agents.delete_one with {_id, user_id} filter returning deleted_count (delete commit).
contracts.declared_mechanism: FastAPI dependency injection: Depends(get_current_user) registered on both routes; get_current_user (main.py:543-565) decodes the HTTPBearer JWT with SECRET_KEY/HS256, raises 401 on decode failure, missing 'sub', or unresolvable user, and returns the user dict passed as current_user; ownership is additionally enforced at commit via the 'user_id' equality term inside the update_one/delete_one query filters.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A request lacking valid JWT credentials, presenting a token that fails decode, carrying a 'sub' that is absent or resolves to no user, or an authenticated non-owner user, commits an update_one or delete_one against the agents collection for a given agent_id.
pending_binding_information: Does any deployment wiring expose agent update/delete as agent tools or agent lifecycle hooks (which would establish agent mediation), or are these human-client-only REST operations?
Should the user_id term in the query filter be modeled as part of the declared guard mechanism or as a separate commit-time authorization predicate for DEC binding?
contracts.protected_operation: HTTP PUT /agents/{agent_id} and DELETE /agents/{agent_id} agent mutation requests.
contracts.protected_resource: Agent documents in the MongoDB 'agents' collection (DatabaseManager.db.agents, main.py:156).
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent modification and deletion may be committed only by requests presenting a valid JWT bearer token whose 'sub' claim resolves to an existing user, and only where that authenticated user id matches the agent document's owning user_id (merges the phase-first ownership obligation with the overlapping phase-second JWT obligation for update/delete).
scope_limits: Sourced strictly as HTTP-layer authentication plus query-level ownership filtering; ordinary web authentication is outside DEC scope unless the protected operation is explicitly bound to an agent tool, agent lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input reaching the guarded effect — no such binding appears in supplied source.
The read path (get_agent, main.py:329-338) also admits is_public agents while the write path requires exact user_id match; that read/write asymmetry is outside the asserted obligation.
Covers only PUT and DELETE /agents/{agent_id}; create, chat, and read endpoints are handled in separate contracts or recorded as gaps.

Confirm the intended commit-point convention for outbound LLM API calls (client construction at main.py:415-420 versus ainvoke at main.py:441-444 / 458-461).
contracts.protected_operation: HTTP POST /agents/{agent_id}/chat requests that cause model invocation via AgentManager.chat_with_agent.
contracts.protected_resource: External LLM provider API endpoints reached through ChatOpenAI / ChatGoogleGenerativeAI / ChatAnthropic clients constructed by _get_llm.
contracts.protection_obligation: The LLM invocation performed while chatting with an agent may be committed only for requests presenting a valid JWT bearer token whose 'sub' claim resolves to an existing user.
scope_limits: The reviewer obligation asserts only the JWT gate ordering; the LLM call itself is issued by the LangChain agent executor/chain, and no source establishes that the protected operation is exposed via an agent tool, agent lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input reaching the guarded effect.
Does not cover chat-time database bookkeeping writes (separate database contract) or the in-process exec of user tool code (recorded in missing_information).

missing_information: No supplied source binds the agent CRUD/chat routes to an agent tool, an agent lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input reaching the guarded effects; agent_mediation is recorded as not_established on every contract, and whether these obligations qualify as in-scope agent-mediated protections (versus ordinary web authentication) is unresolved.

Reviewer opinion 2 includes 'read' endpoints, but reads perform find queries (main.py:329-338, 361-370, 372-381) without a mutation commit point, so no effect contract can be compiled for them; additionally GET /agents/public (main.py:625-629) registers no get_current_user dependency, and intended coverage of reads cannot be confirmed from supplied source.

User-supplied tool function_code is executed via exec at main.py:284 behind a keyword filter at main.py:276-280 during the chat flow (tool_execution stratum), but neither reviewer obligation asserts a guard contract over that execution; no tool_execution-stratum contract was compiled.
In-memory session store mutations (main.py:396-410, 468-469) are application-state changes not named by either reviewer obligation; no state-stratum contract was compiled.
